entry.label: Variety
entry.description: The number of distinguishable possibilities in a specified set. Variety depends on which distinctions are available to an observer for a purpose; it is not a synonym for vague complexity.
entry.canonical_definition: The number of distinguishable elements or possible states in a specified set, sometimes expressed logarithmically; the distinctions and observer must be stated.

profile.title: Variety
profile.canonical_definition: The number of distinguishable elements or possible states in a specified set, sometimes expressed logarithmically; the distinctions and observer must be stated.
profile.summary: Variety counts distinguishable possibilities. A system may have many physical states but little usable variety if the observer cannot distinguish them or the regulator cannot select among effective responses.
profile.why_it_matters: Variety turns vague talk about complexity into a question about differences that matter for regulation. It also makes the observer visible: what counts as a different state depends on purpose, sensing and classification.
key_distinctions: variety vs diversity as a value
historical_lineage: Ashby developed variety as a central cybernetic measure
information theory provided related logarithmic tools
management cybernetics applied attenuation and amplification of variety
practice_connections: separate the variety seen by citizens, frontline workers and management
ask which options can actually change outcomes
do not add reporting variety that no one can absorb
common_misreadings: variety means diversity or complexity in general
profile.editorial_note: Readable orientation and evidence-backed first pass. Not accepted scholarly consensus until named review is recorded.
